title: Advanced Conversation
description: Idioms, storytelling and nuanced opinions for longer conversations.

lessons.title: Idioms & Sayings
lessons.objective: Recognise common Urdu idioms and use a few in conversation.
tips: Idioms rarely translate word for word. Learn the situation each one fits, not just the literal meaning.
Many sayings come from Persian ("Der aayad durust aayad"). Educated speakers use them often; younger people may use them jokingly.

phrases.en: That made my day! (lit. the heart became happy)
(They) drove me up the wall. (lit. put breath in my nose)
the apple of (someone's) eye (lit. star of the eyes)
to build castles in the air
Too many people want the same one thing. (lit. one pomegranate, a hundred sick)

phrases.note: A Persian saying used in Urdu, often teasingly when someone arrives late.

phrases.en: A drop in the ocean / far too little. (lit. cumin in a camel's mouth)
Everyone says something different. (lit. as many mouths, that many stories)
Stop pestering me! (lit. don't eat my head)
phrases.note: Informal and joking among friends and family. Too rude for strangers.

phrases.en: What's familiar is undervalued. (lit. the chicken at home is like lentils)

exercises.prompt: Fifty people applied for one job opening. Which saying fits?
exercises.explain: One pomegranate, a hundred sick: lots of demand for one thing.

context.speaker: Cousin
context.roman: Sorry yaar, traffic bohat tha, aadha ghanta late ho gaya.
context.urdu: سوری یار، ٹریفک بہت تھا، آدھا گھنٹہ لیٹ ہو گیا۔
context.en: Sorry mate, there was a lot of traffic, I'm half an hour late.

options.roman: Koi baat nahi — der aayad durust aayad!
options.urdu: کوئی بات نہیں — دیر آید درست آید!
options.en: No worries — better late than never!

exercises.explain: "Der aayad durust aayad" is the classic friendly reply to someone arriving late.

lines.roman: Mere bhai ne aaj naak mein dam kar diya!
lines.urdu: میرے بھائی نے آج ناک میں دم کر دیا!
lines.en: My brother drove me up the wall today!

lines.roman: Woh har waqt mera sir khaata hai!
lines.urdu: وہ ہر وقت میرا سر کھاتا ہے!
lines.en: He pesters me all the time!

lines.roman: Lekin woh aap ki aankhon ka tara hai!
lines.urdu: لیکن وہ آپ کی آنکھوں کا تارا ہے!
lines.en: But he's the apple of your eye!

lines.roman: Haan, yeh bhi sach hai. Ghar ki murghi daal barabar!
lines.urdu: ہاں، یہ بھی سچ ہے۔ گھر کی مرغی دال برابر!
lines.en: Yes, that's true too. We never value what's at home!

lessons.title: Telling a Story
lessons.objective: Connect events in order and keep a listener engaged.
tips: Linking words carry a story: pehle (first), phir (then), uske baad (after that), achanak (suddenly), aakhir mein (in the end).
"Pata hai kya hua?" (Know what happened?) is a natural way to start an anecdote.

phrases.roman: Mazay ki baat yeh hai ke...
phrases.urdu: مزے کی بات یہ ہے کہ...
accept: maze ki baat yeh hai ke
mazay ki baat ye hai ki

exercises.roman: Main ghar ja raha tha. ___ barish shuru ho gayi!
exercises.urdu: میں گھر جا رہا تھا۔ ___ بارش شروع ہو گئی!
exercises.en: I was going home. Suddenly it started raining!

lines.roman: Pehle main bazaar gayi. Phir achanak barish shuru ho gayi!
lines.urdu: پہلے میں بازار گئی۔ پھر اچانک بارش شروع ہو گئی!
lines.en: First I went to the bazaar. Then suddenly it started raining!

lines.roman: Mere paas chhatri nahi thi, is liye main bheeg gayi. Lekin aakhir mein mazaa aaya!
lines.urdu: میرے پاس چھتری نہیں تھی، اس لیے میں بھیگ گئی۔ لیکن آخر میں مزہ آیا!
lines.en: I didn't have an umbrella, so I got soaked. But in the end it was fun!

lessons.title: Nuanced Opinions
lessons.objective: Weigh both sides, hedge, and disagree respectfully in longer discussions.
tips: Softeners like "shayad" (maybe) and "kisi had tak" (to some extent) make opinions sound thoughtful rather than blunt.
"Baat yeh hai ke..." (The thing is...) buys you time while you think — very natural.

phrases.en: On one hand..., on the other hand...
I'm not sure. / I can't believe it.

phrases.roman: Aap ki baat theek hai, lekin...
phrases.urdu: آپ کی بات ٹھیک ہے، لیکن...
accept: aap ki baat thik hai lekin

phrases.en: I'll have to think about it.

context.speaker: Uncle
context.roman: Aaj kal ke bachche phone ke bina reh hi nahi sakte. Phone bilkul bure hain!
context.urdu: آج کل کے بچے فون کے بغیر رہ ہی نہیں سکتے۔ فون بالکل برے ہیں!
context.en: Kids these days can't live without phones. Phones are completely bad!

options.roman: Aap ki baat kisi had tak theek hai, lekin phone se bachche seekhte bhi hain.
options.urdu: آپ کی بات کسی حد تک ٹھیک ہے، لیکن فون سے بچے سیکھتے بھی ہیں۔
options.en: You're right to some extent, but children also learn from phones.

exercises.explain: Acknowledging the elder's point before adding yours is respectful. Flat contradiction sounds rude to an elder.

lines.roman: Mere khayal mein shehar ki zindagi bohat mushkil hai.
lines.urdu: میرے خیال میں شہر کی زندگی بہت مشکل ہے۔
lines.en: In my opinion, city life is very hard.

lines.roman: Kisi had tak, lekin mera tajurba alag hai.
lines.urdu: کسی حد تک، لیکن میرا تجربہ الگ ہے۔
lines.en: To some extent, but my experience is different.

lines.roman: Baat yeh hai ke ek taraf mushkil hai, doosri taraf bohat mauqe hain.
lines.urdu: بات یہ ہے کہ ایک طرف مشکل ہے، دوسری طرف بہت موقعے ہیں۔
lines.en: The thing is, on one hand it's hard, on the other there are lots of opportunities.

lines.roman: Hmm, is par sochna parega. Shayad aap theek hain.
lines.urdu: ہمم، اس پر سوچنا پڑے گا۔ شاید آپ ٹھیک ہیں۔
lines.en: Hmm, I'll have to think about that. Maybe you're right.

story: Every evening Dada ji tells stories full of old sayings — and now you can join in.

guide.title: Idioms: learn the situation
guide.body: Idioms rarely translate word for word. Learn when people say them: Der aayad durust aayad when someone arrives late; Ek anaar sau beemar when everyone wants the same thing.

guide.title: Telling a story
guide.body: Linking words carry a story: pehle (first), phir (then), achanak (suddenly), uske baad (after that), aakhir mein (in the end). Start with Pata hai kya hua?

guide.title: Disagreeing gently
guide.body: With elders especially, agree a little before disagreeing: Aap ki baat theek hai, lekin… or Kisi had tak… (to some extent).
